Sosnytsya Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Chernihiv Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Sosnytsya's Jews were entirely expelled during the Khmelnytsky uprising, not returning until the early 19th century, when the Chernihiv province joined the Pale of Settlement; the population reached 1,842 (26 percent) by 1897, served by rabbis including Yankel Krichevskiy (1865) and Leiba Berkovich Levitskiy (1883-94). A pogrom on November 15-18, 1905, destroyed 22 Jewish homes and a yeshiva; the community also survived pogroms led by Petliura in 1919. The Jewish population of the Sosnytsya district was entirely destroyed during the Holocaust across three actions on November 10 and 16, 1941 and March 10, 1942, totaling over 300 people shot.
